div.p: Many computer systems, such as those for open system envir onmentsor multimedia servic es, ne edan efcient schedulability test for on-line admission control of new jobs. A lthough various p olynomial time schedulability tests have been propose d, they often fail to decide the schedulability of the system precisely when the system is heavily loade d. This paper presents e cient on-line sche dulability tests which are are shown to be more p r ecise and e cient than any existing polynomialtime schedulability tests. Moreover, our proposed t e s t s can be u s e d for the multiframe model where a task may have di erent computation times in di erent periods. We show the performance of the prop ose dsche dulability tests in several simulation experiments.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: The schedulability test for priorit y-based task set has been extensively studied 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, 13 , 15 , 16 , 19, 21]. Some of them are kno wn to be precise 2,10,19,21]. How ever, precise tests usually have high time complexities and may not be adequate for on-line admission control if the system has a large number of tasks or a dynamic workload. Ecien ton-line schedulability tests are needed for many computer systems with performance guarantee, such as those consider open system environments 3, 8 ] o r time reserv ation 4, 17,18 ], where real-time and nonreal-time applications may b e admitted in a dynamic fashion. E cient on-line schedulability tests are also useful to various service-critical systems, such a s t e l emedicine systems, tele-conferencing systems, and multimedia services that have Quality-of-Service (QoS) re- quirements 22].

In addition to their complexity, many precisetests for priorit y-driven systems require iterative calculations of the task response time in the presence of higher priorit y tasks. It is therefore di cult to develop an intuitiv eunderstanding on how a timing parameter change in one task may a ect the rest of the system schedulability. Closed-form (but imprecise) tests, on the other hands, give a more intuitive reasoning on the e ect of changing certain timing parameters on the system performance. For example, harmonic-period-based schedulability tests 5,6,7] utilize the jitterless behavior among tasks with harmonic periods to increase the accuracy of schedulability. Since many real-time tasks can be designed to execute in any period size, selecting a task period wisely to make it harmonic to other periodswillhave a b i g p a yo in the system schedulability. Similarly, m a n y m ultimedia tasks or control tasks have only several base execution frequencies. By analyzing the system schedulability based only on these basic (or root) p e r i o d v alues, we s h o w in this paper that the system performance can be more accurately predicted.

In this paper, w e present new e cient on-line schedulability tests for both the periodic process model 13] and the multiframe process model 15,16 ]. The major contributions of this work are as follows:

1. We exploit the harmonic relationship of task periods to provide a more precise schedulability t e s t for the periodic process model 13]. The proposed schedulability test not only is much more precise than existing schedulability tests 1,5,6,7,13] but also has an e cient implementation.
2. Our proposed methodology can also be used for the multiframe process model 15, 1 6 ] when a task may have a di erent execution time requirement in di erent periods.

3. Our tests are especially e ective for systems with hea vy loads.As will be shown later in this paper, our proposed schedulability tests are shown to be much more precise than any existing polynomialtime schedulability tests 1, 5, 6, 7, 13 , 15] when the system is heavily loaded.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 provides an overview of well-known schedulability tests and compare their pros and cons. Section 3 presents our proposed precise polynomial-time schedulabilit y test for the Liu&Layland model 13]. Section 4 extends the proposed schedulability test for the multiframe process model 15, 1 6 ]. The simulation results for the proposed schedulabilty tests are shown in Section 5. We conclude the paper in Section 6.

div.head: Overview
div.p: The real-time resource allocation problem has been an activ e researc h topic in recen t decades. Liu and Layland 13] r s t i n troduced the concept of achievable utilization factor to pro videa quic ktest for deciding the schedulability of a set of independent periodic processes with xed execution time and peirod. Under the Liu&Layland (independent) process model 13], the resource requirements of processes are xed in every period, which can be modeled by t w o parameters ( c i p i ). In this model, a task i must be serviced for c i time units per p i time interval. The on-line admission control of a new task i = (c i p i ) can be done in terms of the concept of the achiev able utilization factor 13]:

The schedulability of a set of n processes is guaranteed if the utilization factor of the process set, i.e., U = P n i=1 ci pi , is no more than the achievable utilization factor U(n) = n(2 1=n ; 1) of the Rate Monotonic Scheduling (RMS) algorithm 13], which is an optimal xed-priority s c heduling algorithm. F or the simplicit y of presentation, w ewill use terminologies \task" and \process" interchangeably for the rest of the paper.

The concept of harmonic task periods has been investigated by Kuo and Mok 7] in their study of adaptive system w orkloads. More recently, Han and Tyan 5, 6] proposed new and more precise polynomial-time schedulability tests for the Liu&Layland (independent) process model 13], which w ere shown to be better than the results proposed in 1, 13]. The proposed schedu- labilit y test is based on the comparison with a system consisting only of tasks with harmonic periods.

Although Liu and Layland 13] did provide an O(n) polynomial-time sc hedulability test for on-line admission control, their schedulability test fails to iden tify many schedulable process sets, when the system is hea vily loaded with a number of processes. The schedulabilit y test proposed by Kuo and Mok 7] explored the harmonic relationship of session periods and w as pro ved to bemuch better than the results of Liu and Layland 13]. They show that a process set with periods selected from K fundamental frequencies is schedulable if the utilization factor of the process set is no more than U(K) = K(2 1=K ;1). Note that the number of fundamental frequencies in a system is much smaller than the number of processes. We should point out the schedulability test has a time complexity O(n 5=2 ).

The schedulability test also quickly deteriorates when the number of fundamental frequencies increases, or when the system is heavily loaded. Recently, Han and T yan 5] proposed a more precise polynomial-time schedulability test, which w ere sho wn to be better than the results proposed in 1, 13]. The proposed schedulability test is based on the transformation of process periods into a special pattern, i.e., a single fundamental frequency. For example, p 0 i = r 2 blog(pi=r)e , where p i and p 0 i are the original and new periods of each process i , respectively. The selection of r must minimize the increase of the utilization factor after transformation. If the transformed process set is schedulable, then the original process set is schedulable. Since the periods of the transformed process set form a single fundamental frequency, the original process set is schedulable if the utilization factor of the transformed process set is no more than 100%.

F or example, process set T, shown in T able 1,has three candidates for r under the tests in 5], where r 2 f p i =2 dlog2(pi=p1)e g. T able 1 shows the transformed 0-7695-0713-1/00 $10.00 ã 2000 IEEE periodp 0 i of eac h process when a di erent r is selected. Obviously, r = 2:5 and 3 result in the minimum increase of the utilization factor, and the original process set is schedulable because the utilization factor of the transformed process set is no more than 100%. As astute readers may point out, the transformation proposedby H a n a n d T yan 5] usually results in the significan t increase of processor utilization and damage the preciseness of their proposed schedulability test, especially at heavy system load. F urthermore, the schedulabilit y test is quite complicated and has a time complexit yO(n 2 ) for a system of n tasks and can not be implemented with an incremental algorithm because of the recalculation of the special base and, most importantly, the procedure in minimizing the increase of utilization factor.

In the follo wing sections, w e shall propose a polynomial-time schedulability test which is more precise and e cient than existing polynomial-time tests 1, 5, 7, 13]. We will then extend our results to the multiframe process model 15,16] when a task may have a di erent execution time requirement in di eren t periods.

We n o w extend our result in the last section to processes with varying timing requirements in di erent frames (or periods), such a s m ultimedia sessions. One example is V CDmovies that are often MPEG-1 encoded. MPEG-1 encoded video streams usually consist of a sequence of groups of pictures, and each group of pictures consists of 15 frames with the following pattern: I, B,B,P ,B,B,P ,B,B,P ,B,B,P ,B,B, I 11].

The multiframe model proposed by Mok and Chen 15, 16] provides a better analysis model to exploit the schedulability of processes with variations in their timing constraints. They show ed that the proposed schedulability test is much more precise than the schedulability test proposed in 13], when the execution time of a process varies sharply from frame to frame 15,16 ]. Unfortunately, the schedulability test proposed in 15,16 ] does not consider the harmonic relationship of process periods. As a result, schedulable but heavily loaded process sets are di cult to be identi ed by the schedulability test proposed in 15, 1 6 ], where many computer systems, such a s m ultimedia servers, are often heavily loaded. Note that any multiframe-based schedulability test based on period transformation methods, such a s DCT and S rin 5, 6 ] , will also have di culty in indentifying schedulable but hea vilyloaded process sets because of the same reason in the schedulability analysis of the Liu&Laylandbased process set. The transformation methods usually result in the sharp increase of processor utilization and seriously damage the preciseness of the proposed schedulability test at hea vy orev en moderate system load 9].

div.head: Data Set and Measurement
div.p: The primary performance metric used is the ratio of process sets guaranteed to be schedulable by each schedulability test, referred to as Guarantee R atio. Let n be the number of process sets randomly generated in the simulation, and m the number of process sets guaranteed to be schedulable by a s c hedulability test. The Guarantee R atio of the sc hedulabilit y t e s t i s m n . The test data sets were generated by a random number generator. The number of processes per process set w as randomly c hosen betwe e n 1 0 a n d 3 0 , a n d t h e n umber of fundamental frequencies was bet w een 1 4 and 1 10 of the n umber of processes in the process set. The experiments started with process sets of a utilization factor equal to 70% and increased by 5 % a t a t i m e u n til the utilization factor was equal to 95% (when multiframe process sets were considered, the experiments increased by 5% at a time until the peak utilization factor w as equal to 110%). 400 process sets per utilization factor w ere tested.The utilization factor of each process was no more than 20% of the total utilization factor of the process set. Each process w asassigned fundamental frequencies randomly, and the probability of assigning i fundamental frequencies to a process was 1 2 i;1 . The average r in the root-based schedulability test is 3:329, while the average r in the original process sets is about 2:135.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: This paper proposes e cient on-line schedulability tests which consider not only the harmonic relationship of process periods but also the variance of computation times in di erent periods. The proposed schedulability tests are shown to be much more precise and ecien t than existing polynomial-time schedulability tests 1, 5 , 6 , 7 , 1 3 , 1 5 , 1 6 ]. Unlike m a n y other polynomialtime schedulability tests, the proposed schedulability 0-7695-0713-1/00 $10.00 ã 2000 IEEE tests perform consistently w ell,regardless of whether the system is lightly or hea vily loaded! The soundness of the proposed methodology is veri ed by a series of simulation experiments. The experimental results clearly show the merit of this methodology.

With the adv anceof softw areand hardware technologies, there is an increasing demand to study the real-time resource allocation problems for di erent architectural assumptions and computation models. F or future research, we will extend the reduced-set methodology to analyze the schedulability of \mixed" real-time systems consisting of hard, soft, and rm real-time processes and explore di erent guarantee lev els for di erent kinds of processes. We will also further explore the application semantics of multimedia systems to impro ve the capacit y of the systems in resource allocation.
